course.summary.value: Start with a clear request. Learn to observe, test and improve the result.

lesson.title.value: From an idea to a testable request

lesson.summary.value: Prepare a request, try it in your tool and learn to ask for evidence. This lesson does not publish a website yet.

competency.scope.outcome.value: Describe a small deliverable for a defined audience.

competency.context.outcome.value: Write a request with a goal, context, limits and a test.

competency.evidence.outcome.value: Distinguish a tool's response from an observed result.

competency.repair.outcome.value: Explain the problem and how to check the fix.

competency.transfer.outcome.value: Adapt the same request to the other tool.

tool.claude.value: In Claude desktop, open the Code tab, choose Local and select the project folder. The Chat tab is a different context. The app includes Claude Code; access requires a compatible subscription. Review the response and changes in Code.

tool.codex.value: In the desktop app, select Codex and check the task's folder or project. Send your request in that context and review the response and affected files. Interface labels and layout may vary by version.

notice.self-report.value: Practice outside Ganesha. You run the task in your own tool. Your record is a self-assessment; Ganesha does not verify execution or connect to your account.

example.request.value: I want a page for a fictional music lesson service for beginners. Plan a heading, three services and a contact action. Use fictional data only. For now, do not change files or publish anything. List the plan and three criteria I can test; one must check the contact action.

example.failure.value: Simulated scenario: the request requires a contact action. In the preview, you see “Contact me”, but clicking it does nothing. No real tool has been run here.

sscope.objective.value: Choose an outcome you can check.

sscope.body.value: We will prepare a page for a fictional service. First, ask for a plan. In the planned next lessons, that request can become a tested, published page.

sscope.action.value: Choose a fictional service and finish this thought: who does the page help, and what does it help them do?

sscope.expected.value: A defined audience and main action.

sscope.hint1.value: Think of someone who would visit the page.

sscope.hint2.value: Example: music beginners want to learn about lessons and get in touch.

sscope.criterion.value: You can name the audience and the main action.

sscope.visual.value: Three cards: audience, outcome and main action.

sbrief.objective.value: Include a goal, context, limit and test in one request.

sbrief.body.value: The tool needs to know what to deliver and how you will judge it. Use the example and adapt the service. This field is a rehearsal: nothing is sent to Claude or Codex.

sbrief.action.value: Write your request with the audience, desired content, a limit and an observable test.

sbrief.expected.value: A saved request that another person can check.

sbrief.hint1.value: Replace “make something beautiful” with elements that must appear.

sbrief.hint2.value: Include: plan only for now; use fictional data; explain how to test contact.

sbrief.criterion.value: The request includes all four rubric items.

sbrief.visual.value: A request divided into goal, context, limits and test.

srequest-check.title.value: Check 1: can the request be tested?

srequest-check.objective.value: Recognize a criterion you can test.

srequest-check.body.value: A general impression can guide the style. To check the result, you also need observable behavior.

srequest-check.action.value: Choose the most useful criterion for testing the contact action.

srequest-check.expected.value: A choice with an explanation of the criterion.

srequest-check.hint1.value: Which option describes something you can do and observe?

srequest-check.hint2.value: A test combines a visitor's action with an expected result.

srequest-check.criterion.value: The selected option describes an observable action and result.

check.request.question.value: Which criterion lets you check contact?

check.request.a.feedback.value: This expresses a preference, but does not define how to test contact.

check.request.b.value: Clicking contact shows the fictional address specified in the request.

check.request.b.feedback.value: You can click and compare the displayed address with the request. Both the action and result are observable.

check.request.c.value: The tool should say it is finished.

check.request.c.feedback.value: A completion message does not show whether the contact action works.

check.request.success.value: You chose a testable behavior. Apply the same principle to your request.

check.request.retry.value: Try again: look for an action and a result you can observe.

srun.objective.value: Send the request in the right context and record the real response.

srun.body.value: Open your chosen tool and check the instructions below. Send your planning request. Read the response and compare it with your criteria. If you do not have access yet, save the request and return to this practice later.

srun.action.value: Send the request outside the course. Record where you worked and what you received, without private data.

srun.expected.value: A record of the context, response and something still needing verification.

srun.hint1.value: Before sending, confirm the conversation or project folder.

srun.hint2.value: Write: I asked for a plan; I received these items; I have not opened or tested a page yet.

srun.criterion.value: The record distinguishes what you requested, received and verified.

srun.visual.value: Flow: open tool, check context, send request, review response.

sevidence-check.objective.value: Recognize when execution evidence is missing.

sevidence-check.body.value: Consider this simulated scenario: the tool replies “The page is ready.” You have not opened a file, preview or public address yet.

sevidence-check.action.value: Choose the conclusion supported by the available information.

sevidence-check.expected.value: A conclusion that distinguishes text from proof.

sevidence-check.hint1.value: What have you actually observed so far?

sevidence-check.hint2.value: A tool's claim still needs comparison with the result.

sevidence-check.criterion.value: The answer recognizes the need to open and test the result.

sevidence-check.visual.value: A completion message beside an empty evidence area.

check.evidence.question.value: What can you conclude at this point?

check.evidence.a.value: The website is published and available to everyone.

check.evidence.a.feedback.value: You have not opened a public address. The message does not prove publication.

check.evidence.b.value: All criteria have been successfully tested.

check.evidence.b.feedback.value: There is no record of observed tests. Finishing a request does not prove each criterion.

check.evidence.c.value: I received a claim; I need to open the result and test the criteria.

check.evidence.c.feedback.value: Correct: inspect the result and record what you observe before claiming it works.

check.evidence.success.value: You separated the message from the evidence. This helps you find errors early.

check.evidence.retry.value: Return to the scenario: you only read a message. What check is still missing?

srepair.objective.value: Turn an observed problem into a correction request.

srepair.body.value: Practice with the scenario below. Explain what happened, what should happen and how to test again. This exercise is simulated and does not change your project.

srepair.action.value: Write a request to fix the contact action and repeat the test.

srepair.expected.value: A request covering observed behavior, expected behavior, reproduction and retesting.

srepair.hint1.value: Start with: clicking “Contact me” does nothing.

srepair.hint2.value: Then specify the expected fictional address and ask to click again after the fix.

srepair.criterion.value: The request makes it possible to reproduce the problem and verify the solution.

srepair.visual.value: Four cards: observed, expected, reproduce and retest.

stransfer.title.value: Take the method to another tool

stransfer.objective.value: Keep the goal and adapt the execution context.

stransfer.body.value: Your goal and criteria stay the same when you change tools. How you open the project and inspect the result may change. You do not need a second account to write this adaptation.

stransfer.action.value: Rewrite the context instructions for the other tool. Save your request and record what remains unfinished in the real practice.

stransfer.expected.value: An adapted request and an honest record of your practice.

stransfer.hint1.value: Keep the audience, content, limits and test.

stransfer.hint2.value: Change the conversation or project folder instructions to match the destination tool.

stransfer.criterion.value: The adaptation keeps the expected outcome and identifies the other tool's context.

stransfer.visual.value: The same request linked to two contexts: Claude and Codex.

rubric.request.outcome.value: I defined the deliverable and its main action.

rubric.request.context.value: I stated the audience and required content.

rubric.request.limit.value: I requested only a plan with fictional data, without publishing.

rubric.request.test.value: I included at least one test with an action and expected result.

rubric.execution.location.value: I confirmed the tool's context and sent the request outside the course.

rubric.execution.record.value: I recorded what I received and what I have not verified yet.

rubric.repair.reproduce.value: I explained how to reproduce the problem.

rubric.repair.retest.value: I asked to repeat the test after the fix.

rubric.transfer.preserve.value: I kept the goal, context, limits and criteria.

rubric.transfer.adapt.value: I adapted where to work and how to inspect the result.
